title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete data samples, where traditional deletion or imputation-based approaches lose information or introduce bias. It proposes the proximity kernel, which combines equal-frequency binning, proximity (Voronoi) assignment, one-hot encoding, and a three-level cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding for missing features. Experiments on 12 UCI incomplete datasets show the proposed method achieves the highest average NMI of 0.4245, best or second-best NMI on 10 of 12 datasets, and linear time complexity in the number of samples.

approach: Reimplement the proximity kernel from the paper for the target claim C1 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset. For each feature, equal-frequency binning uses evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values only, then each observed value is assigned to its nearest bin center and encoded as a one-hot vector. Missing feature encodings are filled by a three-level cascading fallback (intersection matching, union matching, global prior) using kernel mean embedding over matching samples. The resulting representation Z is clustered with sklearn KMeans using the ground-truth number of clusters, NMI is averaged over 10 random seeds, and nbins is searched over {2,3,4,6,8} by mean NMI. Finally, reproduce.py writes results/metrics.json comparing the selected NMI to the target 0.2289 within ±0.02.
steps: Setup: confirm numpy, pandas, scikit-learn are installed. No extra packages are required because pandas can read the UCI URL directly. Set all random seeds via the seed lists in config.

Implement src/data.py: read https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data with pandas.read_csv(header=None, na_values=['?', '']); X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).values; y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).values - 1; assert X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), len(np.unique(y)) == 2; return X, y, K=2.

Implement src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins(X, nbins): for each feature j, obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]; if len(obs) == 0, centers = None and prior = uniform 1/nbins; else centers = np.percentile(obs, 100*np.arange(1, nbins+1)/(nbins+1), method='linear'); store centers and global prior frequencies.

Implement proximity_kernel.py assign_bins(X, centers): for each observed value, k = np.argmin(np.abs(x - centers)); tie breaks to lowest index; store integer bin assignments B (n, d) with -1 for missing entries.
Implement proximity_kernel.py encode_observed(B, nbins): build H_obs (n, d, nbins) with H_obs[i, j, B[i, j]] = 1 for observed entries, zeros for missing entries.

Implement proximity_kernel.py compute_fallback_encodings(X, B, H_obs, centers, nbins): for each missing entry (i, j), let O_i = observed features of i and B_i = B[i, O_i]. Level 1: S1 = {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l] for all l in O_i}; S1_j = {m in S1 : X[m, j] observed}; if S1_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S1_j). Level 2: if S1_j empty, S2 = union_{l in O_i} {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l]}; S2_j = {m in S2 : X[m, j] observed}; if S2_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S2_j). Level 3: if S2_j empty, h = global prior for feature j (bin frequencies among observed values, or uniform 1/nbins if feature entirely missing). Store H[i, j] = h and record level counts.

Implement proximity_kernel.py build_representation(X, nbins): call fit_bins, assign_bins, encode_observed, compute_fallback_encodings; concatenate H[i, j] across j to get Z (n, d*nbins); return Z and diagnostics including missing entry count and level 1/2/3 counts.
Implement proximity_kernel.py proximity_kernel(Z): return K = Z @ Z.T / d where d = 19; use only for symmetry and bounds checks.

Implement src/cluster.py evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds): for each seed, run KMeans(n_clusters=K, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit(Z); labels = kmeans.labels_; nmi = normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels); return mean, std, per-seed list.

Implement src/cluster.py search_nbins(X, y, K, nbins_grid, seeds): for each nbins in nbins_grid, call build_representation, evaluate_nbins, and record mean/std/per-seed; select best nbins as the one with highest mean NMI; return best_nbins, best_mean, all_results.

Implement reproduce.py: parse optional --smoke flag. If smoke, load data, subset first 20 rows, run build_representation with nbins=2, assert Z.shape == (20, 38), assert no NaN/inf, assert each observed-feature one-hot sums to 1 and each missing-feature fallback vector sums to 1, compute K and assert symmetry and diagonal <= 1, run one KMeans with seed 0, print NMI and diagnostics. Otherwise run search_nbins on full Hepatitis with nbins_grid and seeds.
Run smoke test: python reproduce.py --smoke. Verify output shows correct shapes, no NaNs, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, and a valid NMI in [0, 1].

Run intermediate checks before full run: print X shape (155, 19), y shape (155,), class counts, total missing entries and per-feature missing counts; verify bin centers are strictly increasing for features with observed values; verify B indices are in [0, nbins-1]; verify H row sums per feature are 1 for all samples; print fallback level counts (level 3 should be rare, <5% of missing entries); verify K is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, K_ij in [0, 1]; run a sanity baseline KMeans on median-imputed raw features and record its NMI for reference.
Run full reproduction: python reproduce.py. This runs 5 nbins values × 10 seeds = 50 KMeans runs on 155 samples; each run is seconds or less.

Inspect results/metrics.json: check the C1 value, best_nbins, per-nbins means, and per-seed NMI spread. Compare |value - 0.2289| <= 0.02. If outside tolerance, run sensitivity variants: (a) percentile centers at 100*(k-0.5)/nbins; (b) percentile centers at 100*k/nbins; (c) kernel K-means assigning each point to the cluster maximizing average K to cluster members. Record each variant's value and choose the most faithful documented variant; otherwise keep the primary result.
Finalize results/metrics.json with the chosen C1 value, target 0.2289, tolerance 0.02, pass/fail boolean, best nbins, per-nbins and per-seed results, diagnostics, runtime, and environment metadata.

Class balance: print counts of y == 0 and y == 1 (expected approximately 32/123 for Hepatitis; exact counts are fine).
Missingness: total number of NaN entries and per-feature NaN counts; confirm common UCI missing markers '?' were converted to NaN.
Binning: for each feature with observed values, the nbins bin centers are strictly increasing; for any entirely missing feature, uniform prior is used.
Proximity assignment: all non-missing bin indices B[i, j] are in [0, nbins-1]; missing entries are -1.
One-hot encoding: for every sample and every feature, the encoding vector h_{i,j} sums to 1 (exactly 1 for observed, probabilities summing to 1 for missing).

Sanity baseline: KMeans on raw features with median imputation gives some NMI; record it to ensure the proximity kernel result is not identical to a trivial imputation baseline.
Parameter count: Z has shape (155, 19*nbins); for nbins in {2,3,4,6,8} this is 38, 57, 76, 114, 152 features.

"""Data loading for the UCI Hepatitis dataset (claim C1, Table 2 of the paper).

Table 2 of arXiv:2510.13352 describes Hepatitis as: 155 samples, 19 features
(13 categorical / 6 numerical), 5.67% missing values, 2 classes.

All values in the raw UCI file are numeric codes ('?' marks a missing value),
so no separate categorical encoding is needed (assumption A1: features are used
as raw integer/float codes, no scaling).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import urllib.request

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# Primary UCI location plus fallbacks (UCI has reorganised its site over time).
DATA_URLS = [
    "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data",
    "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/46/hepatitis.zip",
]

N_ROWS, N_FEATURES, N_CLASSES = 155, 19, 2


def _cache_paths(cache_dir: str | None) -> list[str]:
    if not cache_dir:
        return []
    return [
        os.path.join(cache_dir, "hepatitis.data"),
        os.path.join(cache_dir, "hepatitis", "hepatitis.data"),
    ]


def _validate_text(text: str) -> bool:
    """The raw file must have 155 comma-separated rows with 20 fields."""
    lines = [ln for ln in text.strip().splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    if len(lines) != N_ROWS:
        return False
    for ln in lines:
        parts = ln.split(",")
        if len(parts) != N_FEATURES + 1:
            return False
        if parts[0].strip() not in {"1", "2"}:
            return False
    return True


def _fetch_raw(cache_dir: str | None) -> str:
    """Return the raw hepatitis.data text, downloading it if not cached."""
    if cache_dir:
        for p in _cache_paths(cache_dir):
            if os.path.isfile(p):
                text = open(p, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
                if _validate_text(text):
                    print(f"[data] using cached {p}")
                    return text

    import io
    import zipfile

    last_err = None
    for url in DATA_URLS:
        try:
            print(f"[data] downloading {url}")
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=60) as r:
                blob = r.read()
            if url.endswith(".zip"):
                with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(blob)) as zf:
                    name = next(
                        n for n in zf.namelist() if n.lower().endswith(".data")
                    )
                    text = zf.read(name).decode("utf-8", "replace")
            else:
                text = blob.decode("utf-8", "replace")
            if _validate_text(text):
                if cache_dir:
                    os.makedirs(cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
                    out = os.path.join(cache_dir, "hepatitis.data")
                    with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                        f.write(text)
                    print(f"[data] cached raw file to {out}")
                return text
            print(f"[data] downloaded file failed validation from {url}")
        except Exception as e:  # try the next mirror
            last_err = e
            print(f"[data] download failed: {e}")
    raise RuntimeError(f"Could not obtain hepatitis.data (last error: {last_err})")


def load_hepatitis(cache_dir: str | None = None):
    """Load Hepatitis as X (155, 19) float with NaN for missing, y (155,) int.

    Returns (X, y, K, meta).
    """
    text = _fetch_raw(cache_dir if cache_dir is None else cache_dir)
    df = pd.read_csv(
        io.StringIO(text) if False else _as_buffer(text),
        header=None,
        na_values=["?"],  # UCI missing marker (assumption A6)
        keep_default_na=True,
    )
    # sanity: 20 columns = class + 19 features
    assert df.shape == (N_ROWS, N_FEATURES + 1), f"unexpected shape {df.shape}"

    y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).to_numpy()  # {1, 2}
    X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).to_numpy()
    X[np.isnan(X)] = np.nan  # already NaN via na_values; keep explicit

    assert X.shape == (N_ROWS, N_FEATURES), X.shape
    assert y.shape == (N_ROWS,)
    classes = np.unique(y)
    assert classes.size == N_CLASSES, classes

    meta = {
        "name": "Hepatitis",
        "source": "UCI Machine Learning Repository (dataset id 46)",
        "n_samples": int(X.shape[0]),
        "n_features": int(X.shape[1]),
        "n_classes": int(classes.size),
        "class_counts": {int(c): int((y == c).sum()) for c in classes},
        "n_missing": int(np.isnan(X).sum()),
        "missing_rate_pct": float(100.0 * np.isnan(X).mean()),
        "per_feature_missing": {
            int(j): int(np.isnan(X[:, j]).sum()) for j in range(X.shape[1])
        },
        "cache_dir": cache_dir,
    }
    return X, y, int(classes.size), meta


def _as_buffer(text: str):
    import io

    return io.StringIO(text)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys

    cd = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
    X, y, K, meta = load_hepatitis(cd)
    print("X", X.shape, "y", y.shape, "K", K)
    print("class counts", meta["class_counts"])
    print("missing", meta["n_missing"], f"{meta['missing_rate_pct']:.2f}%")
    if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "--head":
        print(X[:5])

"""Proximity kernel for incomplete data (arXiv:2510.13352, Section 4).

Implements, faithfully to the equations:
  * Eq. (4)  : bin centers c_{j,k} = percentile(X_obs,j, (k-1)*100/(nbins-1)),
               k = 1..nbins  (so c_1 = min and c_nbins = max of observed values).
  * Eq. (5)  : proximity assignment b_{i,j} = argmin_k |x_{i,j} - c_{j,k}|.
  * Eq. (6-7): one-hot encoding per feature, concatenated across features.
  * Eq. (8-14): three-level cascading fallback (intersection -> union -> global
               prior) with kernel mean embedding averages of observed one-hot
               vectors.
  * Eq. (15-16): K = (1/d) Z Z^T.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np


def fit_bins(X: np.ndarray, nbins: int):
    """Eq. (4): per-feature bin centers from observed values only.

    Returns (centers, observed_masks):
      centers[j] : np.ndarray (nbins,) bin centers for feature j (None if the
                   feature has no observed value),
      observed_masks[j] : bool array marking observed entries of feature j.
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    centers: list = []
    observed_masks = []
    # evenly-spaced percentiles in [0, 100]; k-1 = 0..nbins-1 (Eq. 4)
    pct = (np.arange(nbins) * 100.0) / (nbins - 1) if nbins > 1 else np.array([50.0])
    for j in range(d):
        obs_mask = ~np.isnan(X[:, j])
        observed_masks.append(obs_mask)
        obs = X[obs_mask, j]
        if obs.size == 0:
            centers.append(None)  # entirely missing feature (assumption A7)
        else:
            centers.append(np.percentile(obs, pct, method="linear"))
    return centers, observed_masks


def assign_bins(X: np.ndarray, centers: list) -> np.ndarray:
    """Eq. (5): proximity assignment of observed values to the nearest center.

    Returns B (n, d) int with entries in [0, nbins-1] and -1 for missing.
    Ties break to the lowest bin index (np.argmin, assumption A3).
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    nbins = len(centers[0]) if centers[0] is not None else 1
    B = np.full((n, d), -1, dtype=int)
    for j in range(d):
        c = centers[j]
        if c is None:
            continue  # nothing observed for this feature
        dist = np.abs(X[:, j][:, None] - c[None, :])  # (n, nbins)
        b = np.argmin(dist, axis=1)  # NaN rows -> argmin picks 0; fixed below
        b[~(~np.isnan(X[:, j]))] = -1
        B[:, j] = b
    return B


def bin_members(B: np.ndarray, nbins: int) -> list:
    """For each feature j, list of boolean masks: members[j][k] = samples whose
    feature j is observed and assigned to bin k (used for C_{i,j}, Eq. 8)."""
    n, d = B.shape
    members = []
    for j in range(d):
        m = [B[:, j] == k for k in range(nbins)]
        members.append(m)
    return members


def global_priors(B: np.ndarray, nbins: int) -> list:
    """Eq. (13): p_{j,k} = (# samples in bin k for feature j) / (# observed)."""
    n, d = B.shape
    priors = []
    for j in range(d):
        obs = B[:, j] >= 0
        cnt = obs.sum()
        p = np.zeros(nbins)
        if cnt > 0:
            for k in range(nbins):
                p[k] = np.count_nonzero(B[:, j] == k) / cnt
        else:
            p[:] = 1.0 / nbins  # entirely missing feature (assumption A7)
        priors.append(p)
    return priors


def encode_observed(B: np.ndarray, nbins: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Eq. (6): one-hot encodings for observed entries; zeros for missing."""
    n, d = B.shape
    H_obs = np.zeros((n, d, nbins), dtype=float)
    for j in range(d):
        obs = B[:, j] >= 0
        H_obs[obs, j, B[obs, j]] = 1.0
    return H_obs


def cascading_fallback(B: np.ndarray, nbins: int, priors: list, members: list):
    """Section 4.2: fill missing encodings with the 3-level cascading strategy.

    Returns (H, level_counts) where H has the same layout as encode_observed
    output but with fractional distributions in place of zero rows for missing
    entries.  level_counts = [level1, level2, level3] over missing entries.
    """
    n, d = B.shape
    missing = B < 0
    H = encode_observed(B, nbins)
    levels = np.zeros(3, dtype=int)
    prior_matrix = np.stack([priors[j] for j in range(d)])  # (d, nbins)

    for i in range(n):
        O_i = np.flatnonzero(B[i] >= 0)  # observed features of sample i
        M_i = np.flatnonzero(missing[i])
        if M_i.size == 0:
            continue
        if O_i.size == 0:
            # no observed features: nothing to match on -> global prior (L3)
            for j in M_i:
                H[i, j] = priors[j]

"""Clustering evaluation (Section 5.1 protocol).

K-means with the ground-truth number of clusters on the proximity-kernel
representation Z (Eq. 19 in the paper), NMI metric, 10 repetitions averaged,
and the nbins hyperparameter searched over the paper's grid {2, 3, 4, 6, 8}.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.metrics import normalized_mutual_info_score
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer

NBINS_GRID = [2, 3, 4, 6, 8]  # Section 5.1 (requirement R12)
N_RUNS = 10  # Section 5.1: "Each experiment was conducted 10 times"
RANDOM_STATES = list(range(N_RUNS))  # assumption A4
KMEANS_N_INIT = 10  # assumption A4


def kmeans_nmi(Z: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, K: int, random_state: int) -> float:
    km = KMeans(
        n_clusters=K,
        init="k-means++",
        n_init=KMEANS_N_INIT,
        random_state=random_state,
    )
    labels = km.fit_predict(Z)
    return float(normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels))


def evaluate_nbins(Z: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, K: int) -> dict:
    """Run K-means N_RUNS times and average NMI (R10, R11)."""
    per_seed = [kmeans_nmi(Z, y, K, s) for s in RANDOM_STATES]
    return {
        "per_seed": per_seed,
        "mean": float(np.mean(per_seed)),
        "std": float(np.std(per_seed)),
        "min": float(np.min(per_seed)),
        "max": float(np.max(per_seed)),
    }


def search_nbins(X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, K: int, build_representation,
                 nbins_grid=None, verbose: bool = True) -> dict:
    """Search nbins over the grid; select by highest mean NMI (assumption A9)."""
    grid = list(nbins_grid) if nbins_grid is not None else list(NBINS_GRID)
    results = []
    for nbins in grid:
        rep = build_representation(X, nbins)
        ev = evaluate_nbins(rep["Z"], y, K)
        rep.pop("H", None)  # keep results small
        entry = {"nbins": nbins, "z_dim": int(rep["Z"].shape[1]),
                 "levels": [int(v) for v in rep["levels"]], **ev}
        results.append(entry)
        if verbose:
            print(f"[search] nbins={nbins:>2}  Z:{rep['Z'].shape}  "
                  f"NMI mean={ev['mean']:.4f} std={ev['std']:.4f} "
                  f"(min {ev['min']:.4f} / max {ev['max']:.4f})  "
                  f"levels L1/L2/L3={entry['levels']}")
    best = max(results, key=lambda r: r["mean"])
    return {"best_nbins": int(best["nbins"]), "best_mean": best["mean"],
            "best_per_seed": best["per_seed"], "results": results,
            "grid": grid}


def median_imputation_baseline(X: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, K: int) -> dict:
    """Sanity baseline: median imputation then K-means on raw features."""
    Xi = SimpleImputer(strategy="median").fit_transform(X)
    ev = evaluate_nbins(Xi, y, K)
    return {"mean": ev["mean"], "std": ev["std"], "per_seed": ev["per_seed"]}

audit_summary: The clean re-run computes NMI 0.228909... on full UCI Hepatitis (155x19, K=2), matching C1's 0.2289 within 9e-6. The code implements the paper pipeline: per-feature percentile bin centers, nearest-center one-hot encoding, three-level intersection/union/prior fallback, normalized inner-product kernel, and transductive K-means with ground-truth K over 10 seeds and the {2,3,4,6,8} nbins grid. No target scale-down is present; the reported value is derived from data, and PAPER_TARGET=0.2289 is used only for pass/fail comparison. The main caveats are the logged assumptions (categorical integer codes A1, percentile interpolation/scheme A2/A13, restricting KME matches to samples observed on the missing feature A8/A14) and R13: linear-time complexity is not demonstrated and the fallback is naively O(n^2 d) worst-case. requirement_check.evidence: fit_bins builds per-feature centers only from observed values using ~np.isnan(X[:,j]) masks.
np.percentile(obs, pct, method='linear') with pct=(k-1)*100/(nbins-1), i.e. evenly-spaced percentiles; logged as A2/A13.
assign_bins uses argmin |x - c| for nearest-center assignment; np.argmin gives lowest-index tie break and missing values are set to -1.
encode_observed constructs one-hot H (n,d,nbins) and build_representation reshapes it to Z (n,d*nbins).
cascading_fallback implements Level 1 intersection S1, Level 2 union S2, and Level 3 global prior, recording per-level counts.
Level 1 uses mean H[cand1,j] with cand1 = S1 & feature-j-observed; the observed-feature restriction is logged in A8/A14.
When no Level-1 candidate exists, Level 2 uses mean H[cand2,j] with cand2 = S2 & feature-j-observed.
If no L1/L2 candidate exists, H[i,j]=prior_matrix[j] from global_priors; implemented but not exercised on Hepatitis (L3 count 0).
proximity_kernel_matrix computes K=(Z @ Z.T)/d, matching Eq.15 normalized inner product.
kmeans_nmi uses sklearn KMeans(n_clusters=K, init='k-means++', n_init=10) on Z and normalized_mutual_info_score against y.
evaluate_nbins averages over RANDOM_STATES=0..9; metrics per_seed contains 10 runs.
NBINS_GRID=[2,3,4,6,8]; search_nbins evaluates all five values and selects highest mean NMI (A9).
No scaling/complexity experiment is run; cascading_fallback uses per-sample loops over all samples for S1/S2, giving worst-case O(n^2 d), not the paper's claimed O(nd + d n log n).
